video_overlay_text_observed: Caption-card title: "5 reasons why I think Jeffrey Epstein is still alive." Caption: "See you in ValHELLa #standup #standupcomedy #fortnite."
audio_content_summary: Standup comedy set by Sammy Obeid — a satirical 'five reasons Epstein is still alive' bit. The comedy is built around real, documented custody-failure facts (guards skipping checks and falsifying logs, cameras not recording, removed from suicide watch / cellmate gone, the contested autopsy) which it then escalates into absurd conspiracy: a body double swapped in (#JimCarrey), a decoy box-coffin sent to a hospital while the 'real body' is shipped to Israel, and an Epstein Fortnite account logging in from Tel Aviv after his death.
implied_frame: Editorial split A4/B2/C3 (re-checked twice at operator push-back; 3/1/4 -> 4/1/3 -> 4/2/3). Comedy routine, but more of its core is documented than first credited, and the first two passes under-credited it. In evidence record 2019-epstein-death-custody-001: guards (Noel, Thomas) failed rounds and falsified logs, nearly all SHU cameras not recording, no cellmate after the July 2019 suicide-watch incident (June 2023 DOJ IG report), AND the 'boxes / decoy vehicle / real body in a black car' bit, which is REAL — FBI FD-302 in our own EFTA corpus (Bates EFTA00091322): staff used boxes and sheets to fake a body in a white OCME van so the press would chase it while Epstein's actual body left in a black vehicle. The first draft wrongly tacked on 'this is not evidence of a body swap'; removed as status-quo bias — the act is anomalous and the only reason on record is the staff's own 'thwart the media', with no precedent found. Group B (disputed): cause of death (ME suicide + FBI no-criminality vs. Dr. Baden's homicide doubt) AND body identity (the nose/ear body-double claim vs. the 15-year-old comparison photo / aging per Snopes-FactCheck and the fingerprinting + ME identification in the 302) — presented as weighed, not dismissed. Group C (no primary trace): 'still alive' / 'shipped to Israel'; the confidence-and-hair characterization; and the Fortnite bit, which is affirmatively FALSE — no Epstein email links to any Fortnite account; the viral 'littlestjeff1' account was a recent rename by an unrelated player (Epic/Sweeney debunk, Snopes Feb 2026).
capture_method: Pristine original media + metadata pulled from Instagram's CDN via yt-dlp; delivery webm derived once (VP9 video copied, audio normalized to -16 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP off the source AAC — no re-recording, no in-place re-encode).
